launched_with: a host-side launcher script, not `./bench run`; the resulting pier command is equivalent to what `./bench run --concurrency 32` generates (see `command`), and every rule-relevant parameter is also read back from the job's own config.json (`job_config_rule_fields`)

harness.path: harness/ (snapshot of eval/common + eval/deep-swe at the tag)
harness.note: sha256 of each file above on the eval host equals the copy in this repo. The host launched through run-k.sh, which is run.sh with `--n-attempts ${PIER_N_ATTEMPTS}` added (PIER_N_ATTEMPTS=4); `./bench run` passes --n-attempts 4 itself.

config.note: The host config differs only in comments: its non-comment, non-blank lines hash to c47c5806604646235fa645c4c239b4aee7f5fcaf9ad89506519090c1087b7f90, the same as this file's. api_key is ${ENV:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}; base_url https://api.deepseek.com/v1; context_window 1000000; no max_turns.

dataset.name: datacurve/deep-swe-1-1
dataset.task_limits: task.toml unchanged: agent timeout_sec 10800, verifier 1800 s, 2 CPU / 8192 MB

command: IACODER_BINARY_URL=<binary-url> IACODER_CONFIG=<bench>/configs/deepseek-flash.toml IACODER_VERSION=v0.7.64 IACODER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE=mini-swe-agent-custom IACODER_REASONING_EFFORT=max IACODER_EVAL_DECLARE_DEADLINE=1 IACODER_TASK_OUTER_TIMEOUT_SEC=10800 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=<secret> PYTHONPATH=<bench>/harness/deep-swe:<bench>/harness/common pier run -p <tasks-dir> --agent-import-path iacoder_pier:IacoderPierAgent --model deepseek-flash --n-tasks 113 --n-concurrent 32 --n-attempts 4 --timeout-multiplier 1.0 -o <jobs-dir>
